transformation.object: Sample a value-threshold support without materializing its sorted list, rejecting proposals and pruning only certified nontarget weight levels.
transformation.program: Define C(t)=count_i(w_i>t) for above_count or sum_i(w_i>t) for above_mass, and limit=k or top_p. Target A contains positive-weight indices with C(w_i)<limit. Start low=0, high=1, q=1. Each round draw i categorically from S={j:w_j>low} with probabilities w_j/q, retaining original weights and q=sum_S(w). Scan the full original row to evaluate C(w_i). If it is below limit, return i. Otherwise reject i and choose t=w_i. With paired_midpoint also evaluate m=(w_i+high)/2 under the declared arithmetic: if C(m)<limit set high=m and retain t=w_i; otherwise set t=m. Set low=t and q=sum_{w>t}w, then draw again with fresh conditional randomness. Both cutoffs remove only rejected target classes. Never renormalize the row before computing the next full-row membership certificate, reuse the previous uniform without a proved conditional remapping, or return an uncertified last proposal after a round cap.
transformation.storage: Current low/high, surviving mass, sample and full-row certificate reductions; no explicit sorted support list required.

transformation.object: Multicast into physical CTA payloads while projecting full barriers to two-CTA instruction owners and independently deriving stage-release destinations/counts.
transformation.program: Rank r=x+dim_x*y; instruction-atom owner(r)=r & ~1. For x_column, elected issuers lie at y=0: payload P={x+dim_x*yy:0<=yy<dim_y}; release targets R={2*floor(x/2),2*floor(x/2)+1}; expected arrivals E=dim_y. For x_parity_row, elected issuers lie in the first X atom of each row: P={(x%2)+2*a+dim_x*y:0<=a<dim_x/2}; R={dim_x*y,dim_x*y+1}; E=dim_x/2. For whole_x_row, issuer is x=0 in each row: P={xx+dim_x*y:0<=xx<dim_x}; R={dim_x*y}; E=dim_x/2. For every relation, full barrier owners O={owner(r):r in P}; bitmask form O=(P|(P>>1)) & 0x5555. Arm only the intended full-owner barriers with complete transaction accounting, issue payload to P, and let each consuming atom release R once after its readers retire. Producer waits for E atom completions before stage reuse. Recompute P/O/R/E for the actual fallback dimensions; do not replace O or R with P.
transformation.storage: Per-CTA payload stages and full/empty barrier state with independent rank maps.

entries.title: score partition to value partition exchange

transformation.algorithm: Exchange key-sharded probabilities in a common online frame, then assign complete-key PV contractions to disjoint value-feature owners.
transformation.object: Keep score production partitioned by keys but choose between full-value partial outputs and disjoint value-feature outputs using a shared probability tile and common normalization state.
transformation.program: Initially each of four owners computes QK scores for its disjoint key shard. With full_value_partials, retain each owner's own online reference/mass and a full-feature weighted numerator, then merge all four states before output. With disjoint_value_features, combine the four row maxima with the prior common reference to obtain r_new, derive c=exp(r_old-r_new), and correct the old common mass. Each score owner computes its key weights exp(score-r_new), writes them once to shared P at their original row/key positions, and publishes its row weight sum. Combine sums into one common mass d. After publication, feature owner j consumes the complete shared P across all key shards and V[:,j*Dv/4:(j+1)*Dv/4], applying c to its old numerator before adding P*V. Repeat per key tile. Divide each disjoint feature numerator by the common d at finalization and write it once; no cross-owner output-vector combine is required. Preserve actual exponent base/score units, masked weights and defined V tails. Do not normalize each score shard independently and then concatenate its outputs, or let a feature owner read only its old key shard.
transformation.storage: Per-owner output numerator shrinks by four while shared P and per-tile row-statistic exchange are added.

transformation.algorithm: A floating sum uses exponent-indexed primary/carry collectors instead of one floating scalar.
transformation.object: A floating sum uses exponent-indexed primary/carry collectors instead of one floating scalar.
transformation.program: Represent a partial sum using fold primary and fold carry floating values with an exponent-indexed bin anchor. Before deposit rebin to accommodate the maximum magnitude: shift retained collectors toward lower-priority bins and initialize newly exposed bins. Deposit an input by forced-low-bit floating additions into each primary collector, propagating the residual to the next. The highest-range bin uses the source compression/expansion path. Renormalize primary carry bits into the carry vector before the endurance bound is exceeded. Merge two partial accumulators by aligning bin indices, combining corresponding primary/carry components and renormalizing. Convert to output scalar only after the complete partial merge. Source device dispatch binds fold=3; manually batched unsafe deposits additionally require a declared magnitude bound and bounded count before renorm.

transformation.algorithm: When small unsigned codes are stored in bit planes or packed nibbles, compute the integer dot in that representation and apply row metadata only after the exact code reduction.
transformation.object: When small unsigned codes are stored in bit planes or packed nibbles, compute the integer dot in that representation and apply row metadata only after the exact code reduction.
transformation.program: For bit-sliced codes, sum over plane pairs(i,j) of popcount(A_plane_i AND B_plane_j)*2**(i+j). For packed4b words, separately mask low/high nibble byte lanes and perform two unsigned dp4a operations. A packed1b operand can expand each MSB-first bit into a corresponding unsigned nibble0/1 for the same u4 dot engine, preserving coordinate order. After the integer dot, combine per-row lower/scale and code-sum terms to recover the declared affine-decoded dot; then apply L2/IP/cosine correction and clamp/normalization policy separately.
transformation.storage: Bit-plane dot costs code_bits_A*code_bits_B popcount streams; packed4b uses two dp4a per word; u4 promotion increases binary operand storage4x before MMA. Target engine determines tradeoff.

transformation.program: Initialize code_bits words to zero for each group of 32 codes. For code i set j=(i*code_bits)//32 and r=(i*code_bits)%32. OR its low bits at word j offset r, and, when r+code_bits>32, its remaining bits into word j+1. Unpack extracts min(32-r,code_bits) bits from j and the rest from j+1. Thread t in block b owns codes [1024*b+32*t,1024*b+32*t+32); store only groups within length.

transformation.program: Split a key hash into block-selection and lower pattern bits. Map the upper part to a filter block; derive required word patterns from the lower part. Insertion atomically ORs those patterns into their designated words. Query checks (stored_word & required_pattern)==required_pattern for every required word and ANDs the results across its cooperative layout. Merge equal-policy filters by wordwise OR. Intersection/clear are separate operations with separate concurrency/semantic contracts. Conditional no-op OR may skip already set bits only under a valid memory-access model.
transformation.storage: One hashed block bounds scattered-word footprint; block width and pattern density trade memory/atomic traffic against false-positive rate. Statistical error needs separate analysis, no speed or FPR measured here.

transformation.program: Partition A into four-by-four equal blocks with zero upper blocks and unit lower-triangular diagonal blocks. Compute D_ii=inverse(A_ii) by forward substitution. For each block column j and increasing i>j compute D_ij = -D_ii * sum_(k=j..i-1) A_ik * D_kj. Set upper blocks to zero. Products may use staged matrix contractions, but block dependencies and sum completeness are retained. The source forms adjacent blocks 10,21,32 first, then 20,31, then 30 and stores the assembled lower inverse for its later W/U contractions.

transformation.program: View finite FP32 master bits as high word H and low word L. Store the BF16 model bit word P=H+c where c is one exactly when L interpreted as signed int16 is negative (its top bit is set); store L unchanged as the sixteen-bit remainder. To reconstruct, subtract c from P and concatenate that corrected high word with the unchanged low word. Run the optimizer update on the reconstructed FP32 value, then split its result with the same codec. The remainder is raw low bits, not an arithmetic residual that may be added numerically. This source uses an increment at exact midpoint L=0x8000, including when H is even; it is not nearest-even BF16 conversion.

transformation.program: For each candidate compute a lower bound L. If L>threshold discard it; discard L==threshold only when the declared equality/tie policy permits; otherwise evaluate more terms or a finer code representation and repeat, finally offering the complete score to top-k. Nonnegative partial squared-distance sums are lower bounds when all remaining terms and rounded accumulation preserve monotonicity. Signed inner-product sums are not, so disable early stopping unless a separate residual bound exists. For a short-code estimate with error radius E, use estimate-E only when E is proved conservative for the exact refinement score under all admitted rounding. For a fixed-radius predicate use its declared cutoff and the requested equality policy, without fabricating k retained candidates.
transformation.storage: Can reduce remaining lookup/decode work per rejected candidate; adds bound checks and survivor staging. Check frequency trades branch overhead against wasted late terms; no measured optimum claimed.

In residual_first form R=T*(V-EK*H_in), then Y=EQ*H_in+C*R. In coefficient_first form P=C*T and A=EQ-P*EK, then Y=A*H_in+P*V; P and A depend on Q/K/gates but not V or H_in. transformation.program: Encode each value by the declared descending key. Start with empty prefix and residual target r=p*sum(values). For each most-significant digit (11-bit chunks, final5 or10), histogram only occurrences matching the previous prefix, storing both total mass H[b] and occurrence count N[b]. Traverse bins in descending-value order and choose the first occupied bin b whose cumulative mass through b is>=r. Subtract mass of all earlier bins from r, append b to the prefix and retain its count for the next pass. Count is presence/capacity metadata, never the mass rank. In rescan_original mode filter the original row anew. In compact_if_fits, a pass may copy its complete incoming-prefix occurrences into a private bank only when the known count fits; else read original input and omit that compact output. Following passes still filter by their current prefix within any broader cached incoming prefix. First pass reads original input. After all key bits, decode threshold tau, rescan original coordinates and retain every value>=tau, including the entire equality cohort; normalize by their complete retained mass and cast output. Compaction order is not output order and no boundary-ID subset is selected.
transformation.storage: Mass/count histograms, residual target/prefix, optional two capacity-bounded value banks and final original-row output.

transformation.program: Work in natural scaled-logit units x. Carry a finite reference r and zero-initialized L and optionally O. With constant G=2**weight_gain_log2, the invariant is L=G*sum_seen(exp(x-r)) and O=G*sum_seen(exp(x-r)*v). For each tile choose candidate=max(r,max_finite_tile_logit); running_max selects candidate, while lagged_max keeps r when (candidate-r)/ln(2)<=threshold_log2 and selects candidate otherwise. With chosen r_new, c=exp(r-r_new). Correct exactly the old state by c, then add G*exp(x-r_new) and its weighted values for this tile. Masked elements add zero. A denominator-only extra logit a, such as a zero-valued attention sink, adds G*exp(a-r) to L in the same frame. At finalization output O/L and, when requested, natural LSE=r+log(L)-log(G), or divide that result by ln2 for base2 LSE. With finalize=none expose r,L,O,G together. Storage conversion and fast exp2 lowering are separately admitted implementations, not an exact-floating claim.

transformation.program: For y(x,theta)=A(theta)*x+b(theta) inside the selected region, the first reverse input derivative is g_x=A(theta)^T*g_y. transformation.program: Initialize all rotating receive buffers with sentinel in chosen word. At generation k receive into bank k%B while clearing a different bank protected by the proved peer-skew and output lifetime. Each unique producer writes full vectors with valid data; each receiver polls its local vector sentinel word until changed. Complete all required slots before returning. Clear only the assigned disjoint old-bank range back to sentinel. transformation.program: For r=max(P-Q,0), linear encoding forms the admitted positive difference. Log encoding returns -inf when P=0 or Q>=P; when P>Q, compute log_r=logP+log1p(-exp(logQ-logP)), with logQ=-inf giving log_r=logP. A log-weight consumer may use log_r directly, since exponentiating it recovers r in exact arithmetic. Common residual normalization is a shared additive log shift and may be omitted only when the downstream operation is invariant to it. Preserve a separate explicit zero-total-mass policy.

transformation.program: Allocate problems times descriptors_per_problem aligned descriptor slots. Launch one setup kernel before consumers, with disjoint problem-key writers. transformation.program: Define B(n,t,C)=m+floor((t-m)/C), m=min(n,t). Given original token prefix S_i, segment i starts its chunk records at b_i=B(i,S_i,C). Its live count is q_i=ceil(L_i/C), and record j occupies b_i+j for0<=j<q_i. Reserve capacity B(N,T,C); leave [b_i+q_i,b_(i+1)) unused. A valid previous-chunk state is b_i+j-1 only when local j>0; the first chunk uses its own sequence seed even if b_i>0. Keep dense logical task IDs and actual chunk counts separate from these storage slots. Do not initialize or consume gaps as identity records unless a different algorithm explicitly requires that. Changing C changes starts/counts and requires a coherent allocation/producer/consumer generation.
transformation.storage: Potential holes between segment-local chunk intervals inside one host-known bounded allocation.

transformation.algorithm: Consume a complete contraction prefix before the operand suffix is ready.
transformation.object: An operand generation published in an aligned prefix and suffix, allowing the contraction to begin before all operand columns are written.
transformation.program: Partition the reduction axis into [0,prefix_k) and [prefix_k,K). The producer writes and publishes the complete first region, then continues the suffix. Consumer waits for prefix readiness together with any initial-accumulator dependency, issues only prefix MMA atoms into the accumulator, then waits for the suffix's generation-specific readiness before issuing its atoms into that same accumulator. Publish and acquire operand writes using the backend's required memory/proxy fences and barrier protocol. Retirement of the entire asynchronous read sequence, not the prefix signal, permits operand reuse. If an existing accumulator must be rescaled, that correction finishes before prefix execution and never scales new prefix/suffix contributions afterward.
transformation.storage: One operand generation with two publication regions and a shared accumulator.

transformation.program: For current_tensor, reset amax, reduce absmax over every element of this logical tensor, then produce its FP32 multiplier with the requested epsilon and optional downward power-of-two rounding. A zero selected maximum returns multiplier 1 in the pinned current recipe. For a delayed recipe, snapshot history[0]; select max of the old window for history_max or that snapshot for history_recent. transformation.program: Map each finite FP32 score s to a monotone unsigned 32-bit order key: fold either signed zero to positive zero, complement bits for negative values, otherwise set the sign bit. Emit every key above the score boundary plus boundary keys whose ID is at least that ID cut. If all tied entries are needed, skip the ID passes. transformation.program: Allocate phases private per-CTA tables [peers*warps_per_cta,4] of FP32 and one fresh transaction barrier per phase. transformation.program: Snapshot the conceptual committed prefix length c. Each participant reserves a disjoint range for its batch hits and only writes when that range fits the physical candidate buffer. Collectively wait until all claims and writes are complete. If every range fits, publish the appended count and release input stages. Otherwise sum every batch reservation, restore count=c, discard speculative suffix writes and retry each still-live stage. A stage that fits commits; a stage that does not fit has its reservations rolled back and is processed directly with the complete committed prefix by a semantics-preserving compactor. Only after the whole retry finishes may the input ring be refilled. Speculative writes beyond c are dead after rollback; they cannot overwrite the old prefix.
transformation.storage: Candidate records, input stages and per-worker summaries with explicit live intervals.

transformation.program: For generation t, write the completed per-CTA partial into bank t%2 at a sender-injective slot. Choose counter t%2. In phases t%4 in {0,1}, each CTA leader release-adds +1 and acquire-waits for peers; in phases {2,3}, release-add -1 and wait for zero. transformation.program: For each document/head, form d_f by running local reverse recurrence with zero exit adjoint. The actual entry adjoint is M_f^T*lambda_out+d_f. With head_owner_exchange, send d_f and, unless already saved at that owner, matching transfer maps. Wait before reads. Starting at the final fragment offset d_last (terminal exit adjoint zero), walk fragments in reverse chronological order, publishing the current accumulated adjoint as the exit adjoint of each predecessor before applying that predecessor map/offset. Scatter those boundaries back and wait before local seeded reverse walks. A two-fragment document needs only the last offset, not its unused transfer. With neighbor_hops, the last fragment sends d_last to its document predecessor; at each later hop the receiving fragment applies its own M_f^T*lambda_out+d_f and sends to its predecessor. Enforce the supported hop bound and local map availability. Fragments at document ends use zero exit seeds and can execute their tape walks while transport runs, exactly once. Interior local subsegment adjoints are reconstructed in reverse order from their boundary, with the same map orientation. Preserve document/head identity and matching generation through every pool offset; holes and padded heads are not consumed.

Reconstruct both in the accumulator format before use. BF16 high1 plus low2^-9 recovers FP32(1+2^-9), but more detailed residuals can still round away. The pair improves a numerical checkpoint under its admitted error policy; it is not lossless storage or necessarily fewer bytes.
entries.title: paired arithmetic rounding checkpoint

transformation.algorithm: Save a rounded value and optionally its rounded arithmetic residual; reconstruct before consuming.
transformation.object: Save a high-precision value as a rounded low-precision value and an optional same-format rounded arithmetic residual, then reconstruct in the accumulator format.
transformation.program: Let A be the producer accumulator format, T the smaller checkpoint format, and x the already-finalized A value, including its final output scale. Set h=round_T(x). For rounded_only save h and reconstruct xhat=A(h). For rounded_and_residual compute r=fl_A(x-A(h)), save l=round_T(r), and reconstruct xhat=fl_A(A(h)+A(l)). Save h and l with identical coordinate/generation ownership. The residual is computed from the same x just rounded into h, before releasing that producer fragment. A consumer may stream chunks, reconstruct each chunk, and retain only its reduction partials. Do not add h+l in T, compute the residual after discarding x, or treat the pair as an exact bit codec.
transformation.storage: One or two low-format arrays; the paired BF16 case uses the same bytes as one FP32 array.

transformation.algorithm: Partition final rows across cluster peers and gather weighted raw state partials from distributed shared mailboxes.
transformation.object: Assign disjoint final row owners across three CTAs and combine raw attention partials through row-packed distributed shared mailboxes.
transformation.program: For peer rank r in {0,1,2}, own rows [floor(8*r/3),floor(8*(r+1)/3)). Keep own-row raw numerator fragments in registers; publish nonowned row fragments to the row-packed shared mailbox, together with every row max and mass. Complete a cluster publication join. For each owned row find common max M across the three peers; assign a_s=exp2(m_s-M) only for positive-mass peers, otherwise zero. Let D=sum_s a_s*d_s and b_s=a_s/D when D>0, otherwise zero. Combine each owned feature as sum_s b_s*u_s using its local raw numerator and remote mailbox numerators, then cast/write the result once at the original query/head coordinates. Row-stat weights may be formed redundantly in peers, but output ownership remains disjoint. Do not multiply b_s by d_s again: u_s is unnormalized. If a slice is absent, predicate both publication and consumption consistently; padded output rows do not write. Finish a cluster reader-retirement join before mailbox reuse, alias overwrite or CTA exit.

transformation.algorithm: Quantize each row value downward in a unit set by the maximum exponent and fixed significand padding, then perform exact integer mass scans.
transformation.object: Convert finite FP32 row values to downward integer masses using one maximum-exponent unit, then scan exactly without floating addition order dependence.
transformation.program: Let E0 be the maximum value biased exponent and e0=max(E0,1). For each FP32 value w_i, let e_i=max(E_i,1) and m_i=fraction_i+(2**23 if E_i>0 else0). Set shared real unit Delta=2**(e0-150-fraction_padding_bits), used as an exact analysis/decoder scale rather than requiring a representable FP32 scale. Emit q_i=floor((m_i*2**fraction_padding_bits)/2**(e0-e_i)), using a guarded right shift (oversized shift gives0). Equivalently q_i=floor(w_i/Delta). Preserve original ID/order and scan q_i in uint64 with exact nonoverflowing additions. The decoded mass is q_i*Delta<=w_i; each discarded residual is below Delta. The maximum retains positive mass, so Q=sum(q_i)>0. For a normalized encoded distribution use q_i/Q, not automatically the original w_i divided by Q*Delta. Downstream sorted top-p, CDF sampling, finite integer-to-FP64 comparisons, special rows and optional original-numerator output are separate contracts.
transformation.storage: One uint64 mass per live/padded coordinate and complete prefix totals; original value/ID may be retained separately.

transformation.program: For peer count S and per-thread fragment extent E, peer r owns indices r*(E/S)..(r+1)*(E/S)-1. Each sender s keeps its own shard locally and sends receiver r's shard to r's slot s-(s>r), with thread index innermost in memory. transformation.algorithm: Duplicate complete QK/P locally or partition QK by keys and exchange P, while output feature ownership remains fixed.
transformation.object: Keep two disjoint output-feature owners and choose duplicated complete scores or key-sharded scores with shared weight exchange.
transformation.program: Keep owner j responsible for output features [j*Dv/2,(j+1)*Dv/2). With replicate_full_scores each owner computes the complete QK score tile including every latent/rope component, applies the same logical mask, forms its full online max and casts all exponent weights to T. Each replica accumulates the full rounded-weight mass and contracts all keys for its own value slice. No inter-owner P exchange or denominator sum is needed. With key_shards_exchange, each owner computes one key half, exchanges local maxima and obtains a common online row reference before exponentiating. Correct each old feature numerator and local mass to that frame. Cast local P to the same T, accumulate only that key half mass, and publish the local P half into its original row/key coordinates in shared memory. After publication each owner reads the entire shared P across both halves and contracts all keys for its value slice. At finalization sum the two mass shards once in their common frame; normalize each uniquely owned feature output by that full mass. The replicated path instead uses its already complete mass, never the sum of two complete replicas. Keep latent data alive through both score and value readers; an aliased rope/P region may be overwritten only after all rope readers retire. Empty rows use the declared nondividing branch.
transformation.storage: Key-shard exchange needs a full shared weight tile and one aliased two-owner max/mass table; source can also reuse retired rope storage.

transformation.program: For partition t, start next[t]=0 and retired[t]=0 with exactly P_t workers. Each worker leader claims two initial tickets with atomic fetch-add, stages valid task inputs and shares its tickets within the CTA. For each valid current task, claim one further lookahead ticket, compute and publish that complete task, and advance the private lookahead queue; out-of-range tickets do not access task payload. Stop when the next task is invalid, after draining every valid ticket already owned. Each leader then performs one device-scope acquire-release atomic increment of retired[t], wrapping at P_t. The leader observing previous count P_t-1 resets next[t]=0; the wrapping increment already resets retired[t]=0. No claimer may access next[t] after retirement. The retirement protocol protects counter reuse only; full output visibility and the next invocation still wait for whole-kernel completion. Reuse the now-zero buffer on the same completion-ordered stream/graph generation, or use separate storage for concurrent launches. Dynamic task assignment never changes the arithmetic inside a task.

transformation.algorithm: Contract the softmax Jacobian row center through the saved weighted output, then apply each probability tile locally.
transformation.object: Replace the probability-domain softmax derivative row reduction by a dot product of the saved weighted output and its incoming gradient.
transformation.program: For O_i=sum_j P_ij*V_j and incoming g_i=dO_i, set a_ij=dot(g_i,V_j). Replace D_i=sum_j P_ij*a_ij with D_i=dot(g_i,O_i). Let e_i be the incoming gradient of natural-log LSE when lse_gradient=present and zero otherwise; save c_i=D_i-e_i. Each probability tile forms dZ_ij=P_ij*(a_ij-c_i). A finite zero-value sink has a_sink=0 and P_sink=exp(sink-LSE), so its per-row logit gradient is -P_sink*c_i; sum those terms over rows if the sink parameter is shared. Keep the probability tile's support and row identity unchanged. dV=P^T*g remains separate. Chain dZ through score scale/modifier derivatives before Q/K gradient contractions; c is a row statistic, not a replacement for those chain rules. A base2 LSE output's incoming gradient e2 must first be converted to natural-LSE units as e=e2/ln(2).
transformation.storage: One center per query row replaces a separate probability-domain center reduction; P storage/recomputation is chosen independently.

entries.title: common key translation before attention quantization

transformation.algorithm: Common key translation before quantization with optional row-offset restoration for non-normalized consumers.
transformation.object: Translate every key in a softmax normalization domain by one common channel center before quantization, exploiting row-constant logit-shift invariance.
transformation.program: With none, pass keys unchanged to the selected encoder. With channel_mean, sum valid key vectors per declared batch/head group and divide by the valid key count to obtain mu; exclude capacity padding from statistics. Replace each key K_j by K_j-mu before selecting quantization scales and encoding it. Keep quantization block scopes explicit: a common mu does not require one scale for the whole group. For query q and dot scale a the centered pre-quantization score is x_j-c with c=a*dot(q,mu), so softmax weights and the weighted value output need no c addition. Keep original masks/biases at their logical coordinates; if extra normalization logits exist, shift them by -c as well. If original-frame LSE or unnormalized scores are requested, add c to the centered result exactly once in the appropriate log units; LSE2 uses c*log2(e). Defined empty rows retain their output/LSE convention. Quantized centered keys and quantized original keys are different approximations: require an explicit error policy rather than treating centering as bitwise-transparent preprocessing. Recompute mu when input values change, even if preparation reuses addresses and shapes.
transformation.storage: Shared FP32 key mean plus staged mean partials; quantized key buffers/scales are separate encoder storage.

transformation.program: Replace storage and later reads of the full normalized probability matrix with a saved log-normalizer per logical row. For a tile, recompute its scaled logits x from the unchanged operands. With a natural-log checkpoint L use P=exp(x-L); with base2 checkpoint L2 use P=exp2(x*log2(e)-L2). Explicitly set excluded logical positions to zero, apply admitted probability casts, and feed the reconstructed tile to its consumer before releasing it. transformation.storage: One log-normalizer per row plus the currently consumed tile replaces a full probability matrix.

transformation.object: When multiple CTAs explore one query graph, separate short-lived local candidate deduplication from query-wide atomic ownership of expanded parents.
transformation.program: Give each CTA a local visited table for candidate duplicates, reset/repopulate it as required by the current frontier. Give the query a separate global traversed table retained across iterations. Walk ranked unused candidates; atomically insert a parent ID into the global table. Only the successful inserter marks and expands that parent; a failed claimant invalidates its local copy and considers another. Merge per-CTA retained outputs after search. Local candidate revisit and globally unique parent expansion have distinct lifetimes.
transformation.storage: Per-CTA shared local hash plus per-query global atomic hash and num_cta*32 intermediate results. Local reset saves persistent visitation storage at the cost of repeated inserts.

transformation.object: When a key/value slot cannot be claimed in one atomic operation, separate key ownership from payload readiness and constrain which readers may observe the intermediate state.
transformation.program: Stable path: atomically CAS empty key to desired key; only the successful claimant stores its payload. A reader finding the key must wait until payload differs from its empty sentinel before consuming it. In insertion-only speculative path, perform key CAS and payload CAS back-to-back: key winner retries payload CAS from sentinel until it succeeds; a key loser that speculatively acquired payload clears it back to sentinel, letting rightful winner complete. The speculative path cannot publish a complete key/value snapshot until all insertion participants finish. Whole-slot packed CAS is a separate realization with no split readiness wait.
transformation.storage: Avoids requiring a native wide CAS but adds payload polling or speculative retry/cleanup, with two atomic locations per slot.

transformation.algorithm: One stable digit partition using global bin bases, per-tile count prefixes and local stable ranks.
transformation.object: One stable digit partition using global bin bases, per-tile count prefixes and local stable ranks.
transformation.program: For each digit bin b compute global base(b)=sum counts of smaller bins. Each tile computes its stable rank within bin and bin count. Source may sort into shared memory by full local rank then subtract the tile-local digit base from the global offset. Separate upsweep materializes count prefixes; onesweep publishes PARTIAL digit counts, looks back to a COMPLETE prefix and then scatters within the same pass. The onesweep full-tile all-one-bin shortcut skips local ranking/scatter rearrangement but still completes count-prefix publication. Repeating stable passes from least to most significant digit sorts the complete transformed key.

transformation.algorithm: Stable prefix rank of valid original occurrences, with a matching count or hole-preserving span.
transformation.object: Choose hole-preserving support rows or stably compact valid indexed occurrences into a prefix while preserving original-slot validity and duplicate multiplicity.
transformation.program: For each original row evaluate its validity predicate at original slot s, including source index bounds, segment/causal identity and any caller position limit. With keep_positions, write the already translated valid key/metadata at slot s and an invalid sentinel otherwise; the processing span is last valid slot plus one, or zero. With stable_compact, let rank(s) be the number of valid original slots before s. Write each valid occurrence at rank(s) with its translated key and associated metadata, retain duplicates as separate entries, pad the remaining row invalid, and set processing length to total valid count. Apply no original position cut again to the packed slots. Publish row, length and metadata together. Every consumer, including backward, uses the same prepared representation or an explicitly equivalent occurrence map; keep original-slot labels if a consumer needs them. Do not sort by key ID or deduplicate as an incidental compaction step.
transformation.storage: Prepared indexed support, optional occurrence metadata and one matching row length.

In prepared_workspace, prepare independent chunk/head records EK,EQ,W=K_restore^T*T,P=C*T,E_end without reading H or V, encode each record for the later native readers, finish async stores and publish the complete workspace. transformation.program: Advance the device step counter. Mark all already resident experts required by this step with its age. Process missing required IDs in route order; choose the oldest unpinned slot, then smallest slot ID, evict its old inverse map, install the new expert in both maps, pin it at current age, and append one expert/slot copy plan record. A repeated expert is now resident and creates no second copy. Copy every tensor of each planned expert into the same chosen slot using the plan count read on the device. After the complete copy generation is ready, execute routes using resident slot IDs and original route weights. Inactive routes use a safe slot and zero weight. Do not start a subsequent eviction while prior payload readers remain active.
transformation.storage: Reusable bounded payload slots with explicit generation identity.

transformation.object: Process absolute even/odd token pairs across arbitrary request chunk boundaries using a position-tagged carry and a read-before-commit phase boundary.
transformation.program: For each nonempty request chunk with starting absolute position a, positions are a+i. Emit only odd positions. An odd token after the first chunk row reads its immediately preceding even row from the same request. An odd first row reads old carry only if its tag equals a-1; otherwise emit no pair. Each valid pair invokes the declared processor on its even/odd payloads and retains the odd row output/destination. After all old-carry readers finish, examine the last position: if even, copy that last payload/gate to the stream state and tag it with that absolute position; if odd, invalidate the tag. Empty or inactive requests preserve state. With parallel_read_then_commit use a grid/launch-wide read-complete boundary before commit; an ordinary CTA-local barrier cannot order different output/commit CTAs. A subsequent invocation waits for the complete payload/tag commit. State-ID reuse first invalidates the old stream generation.
transformation.storage: Per stable stream ID, one payload/gate pair and absolute position tag.

transformation.program: Initially retain every valid candidate until at least k exist. After each exact compaction retain k winners and a value threshold no greater than the least winner. Later input values at or below that threshold may be ignored because k retained values already dominate or tie them. Append all surviving value/index pairs; if count reaches 2*k, or final count exceeds k, compact the complete candidates back to k using an exact selector. The count before an append is below 2*k, so capacity >= 2*k+scan_tile admits an all-hit input tile. At end expose k winners. For sharded scans, merging each shard top-k into a final top-k is separate and must include every nonempty shard.
transformation.storage: O(k+scan_tile) candidate value/index pairs per worker.

transformation.algorithm: Remove only structured zeros and encode retained positions for sparse contraction.
transformation.object: Each aligned four-value group is represented by two retained values and a position nibble for a sparse MMA consumer.
transformation.program: For each row and aligned K quartet, find the positions of its at most two nonzero values in increasing order. With two nonzeros retain those positions. transformation.program: Allocate one arrival counter for every allowed local-domain ID and two global family ticket counters. Zero them once for the invocation. Launch at least N0+N1 CTAs with threads/shared memory large enough for either body. Each CTA leader reads its domain ID and increments that domain's arrival counter. If N0<=N1, cycle through floor(N1/N0)+1 tags, preferring family0 on tag0 and family1 otherwise. If N0>N1, cycle through floor(N0/N1)+1 tags, preferring family0 on all but the last tag. Atomically claim a ticket from the preferred family. If it is out of range, claim exactly once from the other family. Broadcast the final family/ticket, join every reader, and only then reuse control scratch for the selected body. Execute that valid job once or exit uniformly if the final ticket is out of range. A CTA does not loop to another job. Preference is a placement heuristic; overflow counters count failed attempts and are not counts of completed work. Wait for whole- grid completion before consuming outputs or resetting shared counters.

transformation.program: Let vector v have block floor(v/32) and lane v%32. For each feature d, store its 32 codes consecutively in code_bits*32/8 bytes; feature planes are contiguous within the vector block. On append starting inside an old block, align start down to32, make lanes before start invalid, pack their values as zero and OR only new fields into existing bytes. Consumer loads each dimension plane cooperatively, shuffles packed fields back to vector lanes and decodes each code for its feature before metric accumulation.
transformation.storage: Stores vector_block*D*code_bits/8 bytes per complete block; cooperative lane rearrangement trades shuffle work for contiguous same-feature loads. Append may revisit a partial block without rewriting its existing fields.

transformation.program: Assign one warp to an input vector. For input tile base J, lane l collects bit b from x[J+l+32*b]>threshold[J+l+32*b], with invalid coordinates zero. Store that lane-local pack in warp scratch. Output-byte lane t reads bit floor(t/4) from scratch lanes (t%4)*8 through (t%4)*8+7, placing them into its output bits0..7. Store byte J/8+t only if within ceil(dim/8). This transposes the32-by8 bit tile while preserving the logical consecutive-bit output format.
transformation.storage: Coalesced warp input loads, one byte scratch per lane and byte stores; transposition adds scratch/shuffle-equivalent work compared with scalar consecutive packing.

transformation.program: For each component k and sample i form Y[i,d]=sqrt(weight[i,k])*(X[i,d]-mean[k,d]). Accumulate C[k]=sum_batches transpose(Y)*Y, using beta0 first then beta1 for subsequent batches. Divide by the explicit denominator, mirror one authoritative triangle and add reg_covar to diagonal. Means and responsibilities are fixed across the centered accumulation pass. Raw second moment minus mean outer product is a separate numerical algorithm, not substituted without its own denominator/rounding argument.

transformation.program: Select exact global top-k from the union of initial per-worker windows and distribute those winner records to their original workers. Let b be its kth value. For the rest of each disjoint shard retain records strictly greater than b; discarded ties are permitted because the retained bootstrap winners already supply k witnesses. A worker can compact its complete local candidates to k once at least k exist; thereafter it may raise its filter threshold to the least local winner. Discarding below either threshold is safe: the bootstrap threshold has k global witnesses, and any raised local threshold has k local witnesses. Finally select exact global top-k over every retained worker candidate, including workers that never reached k locally.
transformation.storage: Candidate records, input stages and per-worker summaries with explicit live intervals.

transformation.algorithm: Gate opposite-operand memory fetch by an exact multiplication annihilator and zero-fill the unchanged dense compute tile.
transformation.object: Replace an opposite-operand load by a zero-filled tile when the corresponding complete multiplication coordinates are certified zero.
transformation.program: For a dense paired-K operand load, inspect both corresponding activation codes. In zero_code_pair mode certify both decoded magnitudes zero; sourceE2M1 byte test(code_byte &0x77)==0 ignores each sign bit only. If certified, issue the original16-byte asynchronous copy with source byte count0, defining the destination tile as zeros. Otherwise fetch all16 source bytes. Keep identical copy commit/wait and dense MMA schedule. Out-of-rangeK tail uses the same zero-fill mechanism only under the declared neutral tail contract. The transformed tile is not an equivalent standalone weight tensor; it is equivalent only in the gated contraction context.
transformation.storage: Same destination stages; opposite operand may need offline pair-major permutation.
